places.name: Alki Point
places.description: Landing site of the Denny Party in 1851, the founding settlement of what would become Seattle. Located on the western shore of Elliott Bay.

places.name: Duwamish River
places.description: River flowing into Elliott Bay, central to Duwamish tribal life and later industrialized as part of Seattle's harbor development.

places.name: Pioneer Square
places.description: Seattle's oldest neighborhood, devastated by the Great Fire of 1889 and rebuilt in brick and stone. The heart of early Seattle.

places.name: Pike Place Market
places.description: Seattle's iconic public farmers market, opened in 1907 to connect consumers directly with farmers. One of the oldest continuously operated public markets in the U.S.

places.name: Harbor Island
places.description: Artificial island at the mouth of the Duwamish River, created in the early 1900s and developed into a major shipbuilding and industrial center.

places.name: Boeing Plant 2
places.description: Boeing's massive wartime factory along the Duwamish River where B-17 and B-29 bombers were produced during World War II.

places.name: Colman Dock
places.description: Seattle's primary waterfront ferry terminal, built by James Colman in 1882. Served as the hub for Puget Sound ferry service for over a century.

places.name: Seattle Center
places.description: 74-acre civic campus built for the 1962 Century 21 Exposition (Seattle World's Fair). Home to the Space Needle, museums, and performance venues.

places.name: Space Needle
places.description: 605-foot observation tower built for the 1962 World's Fair, Seattle's most iconic architectural landmark.

places.name: Bellevue
places.description: City east of Seattle across Lake Washington. Became a major technology hub after Microsoft moved there in 1979.

places.name: Redmond
places.description: City east of Bellevue that became Microsoft's permanent headquarters location, transforming from a rural community to a tech center.

places.name: Medicine Creek
places.description: Creek near present-day Olympia where the 1854 Treaty of Medicine Creek was signed, ceding tribal lands including Vashon Island to the U.S. government.

places.name: Point Defiance Park
places.description: 760-acre park at the northern tip of Tacoma overlooking Puget Sound and Vashon Island, established in 1888. Site of the Tahlequah ferry terminal.

places.name: Ruston
places.description: Small city adjacent to Tacoma, site of the ASARCO copper smelter that operated from 1889 to 1985. Smelter emissions affected Vashon Island for decades.

places.name: Stadium High School
places.description: Tacoma landmark originally built as a luxury hotel in 1891, converted to a high school in 1906 after a fire. Notable for its French chateau-style architecture.

places.name: Tacoma Narrows
places.description: Strait connecting the main basin of Puget Sound with its southern reaches, between Tacoma and the Kitsap Peninsula. Site of the famous bridge collapse of 1940.

places.name: Puyallup
places.description: City southeast of Tacoma, home to the Puyallup Tribe and site of the Western Washington Fairgrounds used as Camp Harmony internment assembly center in 1942.

places.name: Puyallup Fairgrounds
places.description: Western Washington Fairgrounds in Puyallup, used as 'Camp Harmony' temporary assembly center where Japanese Americans were detained in 1942 before transfer to permanent internment camps.

places.name: Tacoma Dome
places.description: Large wooden-domed arena in Tacoma, opened in 1983. One of the largest wood-domed structures in the world.

places.name: Whispering Pines Lodge
places.description: A remote Pacific Northwest lodge on Vashon Island where time moves differently. Built 1910, renovated 1935 by Foresters, operating continuously.

descriptions.1910: Frontier outpost. Raw timber, oil lamps, wood stoves, single great room.
descriptions.1935: Art Deco transformation by Foresters. Geometric details, hidden passages.
descriptions.1965: Family resort. Fluorescent lighting, vinyl, institutional pragmatism.
descriptions.present: Cozy-luxe restoration. Raw timber, Art Deco details, modern comfort.

places.sensoryProfile: Cedar and wood smoke. Warm light through old windows. Constant whisper of surrounding forest.
places.narrativeFunction: The lodge is the series' central character — chooses guests, shapes experiences, holds them until ready.
places.stormBehavior: Every system activates. Boiler accelerates, mirror delays further, corridors rearrange, deeper architecture revealed.

places.name: Room 33
places.description: The threshold room at the lodge's heart. Created by Siobhan's 1915 ritual. Guests during storms may emerge transformed, terrified, or not at all.

descriptions.1910: Standard guest room. Pine walls, iron bed, oil lamp.
descriptions.1935: Post-ritual, Foresters installed compass rose floor inlay.
descriptions.1965: Sealed after 1967 Fink incident. Compass rose papered over.
descriptions.present: Bed, desk, wardrobe with mirror, compass rose on floor. Always cold.

places.sensoryProfile: Cold and silent. Thick absorptive silence. Compass rose on floor. Wardrobe mirror reflects things not present.
places.narrativeFunction: Threshold (between eras), reset (returning transformed), selection (choosing who enters).
places.stormBehavior: Temperature drops. Compass rose may rotate. Mirror shows other eras. Wallpaper shifts between periods.

places.name: The Triangle Bar
places.description: Emotional center — triangular room where Mixie and Flynn tend bar. Every confession, relationship, and story passes through.

descriptions.present: Emotional center — triangular room where Mixie and Flynn tend bar. Every confession, relationship, and story passes through.

places.sensoryProfile: Warm amber light. Cedar, whiskey, old wood. Glasses clinking. Piano in corner. Mirror reflecting a beat late.
places.narrativeFunction: The confessional. Every significant conversation happens here.
places.stormBehavior: Mirror delay deepens. Piano plays untouched. Glasses slide. Atmosphere becomes pressure cooker.

places.name: The Great Room
places.description: Lodge's communal center with massive stone fireplace burning continuously since 1910. Fire's ash contains objects from other eras, collected by Tom.

descriptions.present: Lodge's communal center with massive stone fireplace burning continuously since 1910. Fire's ash contains objects from other eras, collected by Tom.

places.sensoryProfile: Wood smoke and cedar. Crackling fire. Vaulted ceiling with visible timber beams.
places.narrativeFunction: Communal gathering space and anchor point for the lodge's living presence.
places.stormBehavior: Fire intensifies without fuel. Objects appear in ash — buttons, coins, paper fragments from other eras.

places.name: The Lobby & Front Desk
places.description: Illusion of normalcy — competent hotel lobby masking lodge's true nature. Guest ledger contains every name since 1910.

descriptions.present: Illusion of normalcy — competent hotel lobby masking lodge's true nature. Guest ledger contains every name since 1910.

places.sensoryProfile: Grandfather clock ticking. Warm wood and polished brass. Old paper from guest ledger.
places.narrativeFunction: Threshold between the ordinary world and the lodge's deeper nature.
places.stormBehavior: Clock accelerates. Bell rings unstruck. Ledger pages turn on their own. During severe storms, door appears to Mirror Room.

places.name: The Library
places.description: Wood-paneled room with ~2,000 books, Foresters' coded texts, clock synced to boiler. Locked cabinet contains Foresters' records and earlier drafts of Mixie's novel.

descriptions.present: Wood-paneled room with ~2,000 books, Foresters' coded texts, clock synced to boiler. Locked cabinet contains Foresters' records and earlier drafts of Mixie's novel.

places.sensoryProfile: Old paper, leather, wood polish. Quiet except for clock. Warm, amber-lit, enclosed.
places.narrativeFunction: Investigation hub and repository of the lodge's documented history.
places.stormBehavior: Clock accelerates. Candle lit during storm refuses to go out. Books fall open to relevant pages.

places.name: The Dining Room & Kitchen
places.description: Lodge's most practical spaces — grounding supernatural in ordinary. Kitchen resists supernatural influence. Communal table since 1910.

descriptions.present: Lodge's most practical spaces — grounding supernatural in ordinary. Kitchen resists supernatural influence. Communal table since 1910.

places.sensoryProfile: Coffee morning, bread afternoon, roasting vegetables evening. Morning light through east windows.
places.narrativeFunction: Grounding anchor where the mundane resists the supernatural.
places.stormBehavior: Kitchen resists — largely unaffected. Herb garden grows faster. Menu board occasionally shows dishes in unfamiliar handwriting.

places.name: The Service Corridors
places.description: Network of narrow passages. Sound travels impossibly. During storms, carry whispers from other eras and rearrange spatially.

descriptions.present: Network of narrow passages. Sound travels impossibly. During storms, carry whispers from other eras and rearrange spatially.

places.sensoryProfile: Narrow, four feet wide. Damp plaster, metallic tang. Sound distortion. Temperature pockets.
places.narrativeFunction: Liminal connective tissue enabling spatial disorientation and temporal bleed.
places.stormBehavior: Whispers intensify into full sentences. Spatial rearrangement. Earth-floored section near sub-basement warms.

places.name: The Basement & Boiler Room
places.description: Tom's domain. 1935 Kewanee steam boiler modified by Foresters. Concealed hatch to cave system. Boiler accelerates before storms. Steam visions form.

descriptions.present: Tom's domain. 1935 Kewanee steam boiler modified by Foresters. Concealed hatch to cave system. Boiler accelerates before storms. Steam visions form.

places.sensoryProfile: Machine oil, warm metal. Boiler's cyclic pulse like heartbeat. Low ceilings. Hatch vibrates faintly.
places.narrativeFunction: Gateway between the mechanical and the primal; Tom's seat of power and the lodge's heartbeat.
places.stormBehavior: Boiler accelerates before storms. Steam visions form. 1943 death echoes play. Hatch vibrates and warms. Tom's radio tunes to stations from other decades.

places.name: The Storage Rooms (Lost and Found)
places.description: Off service corridors — belongings left by guests who vanished. Tom maintains it like a cemetery. Locked Voss steamer trunk is Season Two mystery.

descriptions.present: Off service corridors — belongings left by guests who vanished. Tom maintains it like a cemetery. Locked Voss steamer trunk is Season Two mystery.

places.sensoryProfile: Old leather and cedar. Absorbed silence — visitors involuntarily whisper. Voss trunk emits faint perfume and pipe tobacco.
places.narrativeFunction: Memorial and mystery repository; physical evidence of the lodge's history of disappearances.
places.stormBehavior: Room warms. Sounds from belongings — latches clicking, clothing rustling, pocket watch ticking. Voss trunk vibrates during Convergence Storms.

places.name: The Whispering Pines (Forest)
places.description: Old-growth Pacific Northwest rainforest surrounding lodge. Trees produce sustained whisper. Trails shift during storms. Forest is lodge's soft boundary.

descriptions.present: Old-growth Pacific Northwest rainforest surrounding lodge. Trees produce sustained whisper. Trails shift during storms. Forest is lodge's soft boundary.

places.sensoryProfile: Every shade of green. Filtered light, perpetual twilight. The whisper — always present, always almost language. Petrichor, cedar, fir sap.
places.narrativeFunction: The lodge's soft boundary and living perimeter; both protective barrier and testing ground.
places.stormBehavior: Whisper becomes roar. Trails shift. Perimeter becomes elastic. Bioluminescence on forest floor. Circle Path becomes visible.

places.name: The Clearing & Fire Pit
places.description: Natural clearing quarter mile south with fire pit ringed by river stones predating European settlement. Lodge's outdoor confessional.

descriptions.present: Natural clearing quarter mile south with fire pit ringed by river stones predating European settlement. Lodge's outdoor confessional.

places.sensoryProfile: Wood smoke. Fire's crackle. Open sky through canopy like natural oculus. Natural amphitheater acoustics.
places.narrativeFunction: Outdoor truth-telling space; the lodge's open-air confessional and ritual ground.
places.stormBehavior: Fire refuses to die. Sound focuses. Sky occasionally breaks above fire pit. Circle Path becomes obvious.

places.name: The Stone Circle
places.description: Twelve glacial erratics in circle deep in forest, thirteenth at center. Oldest intentional structure. Moss grows to perimeter but does not cross.

descriptions.present: Twelve glacial erratics in circle deep in forest, thirteenth at center. Oldest intentional structure. Moss grows to perimeter but does not cross.

places.sensoryProfile: Quietest outdoor space. Forest whisper muted. Diffused light, no proper shadows. Fullness of deep listening.
places.narrativeFunction: Origin point and sacred anchor; the eye of every storm and the lodge's deepest root.
places.stormBehavior: Wind produces low harmonic tone. Carvings appear sharper. Central stone warms. Faint warm light. Inside circle: calm, eye of every storm.

places.name: The Guest Cabins
places.description: Six detached cabins along Shore Path, each with own personality. They drift — shifting position subtly. Named: Cedar, Fern, Owl, Hemlock, Raven, Moss. Owl is Flynn's. Moss retains Siobhan's lavender.

descriptions.present: Six detached cabins along Shore Path, each with own personality. They drift — shifting position subtly. Named: Cedar, Fern, Owl, Hemlock, Raven, Moss. Owl is Flynn's. Moss retains Siobhan's lavender.

places.sensoryProfile: Each cabin has distinct character. Salt air from shore. Wood and forest scents. Isolation within community.
places.narrativeFunction: Individual character spaces providing isolation, privacy, and personal supernatural encounters.
places.stormBehavior: Subtle positional drift over time. Fern produces vivid dreams. Hemlock becomes harder to find at night.

places.name: The Caves
places.description: Branching cave system beneath lodge — oldest space. Three levels: Upper Chambers, Middle Passages, Water Chamber with temporally reflective pool. Deeper you go, less stable time becomes.

descriptions.present: Branching cave system beneath lodge — oldest space. Three levels: Upper Chambers, Middle Passages, Water Chamber with temporally reflective pool. Deeper you go, less stable time becomes.

places.sensoryProfile: Absolute darkness. Water everywhere. Carved walls with spirals and wave patterns. Temperature rises with depth.
places.narrativeFunction: The lodge's deepest source of power; where time itself becomes unstable and the oldest forces reside.
places.stormBehavior: Water flow intensifies. Voices become distinct. Water Chamber pool shows temporal reflections. Deep passages produce echoes of future and past.

places.name: The Subterranean Waterways
places.description: Underground streams threading cave system — lodge's connective tissue. Water carries temporal and memorial properties. Spring emerges in basement at constant 42 degrees. Water is memory.

descriptions.present: Underground streams threading cave system — lodge's connective tissue. Water carries temporal and memorial properties. Spring emerges in basement at constant 42 degrees. Water is memory.

places.sensoryProfile: Sound of moving water throughout cave system, basement, and during storms, building's walls. Cold, mineral-scented, rhythmic.
places.narrativeFunction: The lodge's circulatory system; carrier of memory and temporal properties throughout the structure.
places.stormBehavior: Flow increases. Rhythm accelerates synced with boiler. Sound propagates — cave voices audible in basement. Memory echoes surface near water.

places.name: The Hidden Rooms
places.description: Spaces appearing only when conditions are met — during storms, for specific people, at specific emotional states. Known rooms: Writing Room, Memory Room, Mirror Room, Seventh Cabin.

descriptions.present: Spaces appearing only when conditions are met — during storms, for specific people, at specific emotional states. Known rooms: Writing Room, Memory Room, Mirror Room, Seventh Cabin.

places.sensoryProfile: Warm. Silent like Room 33. Lit by unidentifiable sources. Subtle vibration, as though lodge expends effort to maintain space.
places.narrativeFunction: The lodge's most active expressions of agency; spaces created in response to need.
places.stormBehavior: Hidden rooms appear when conditions align. Writing Room for writers. Memory Room for unprocessed grief. Mirror Room adjacent to lobby.

places.name: The Shore Path
places.description: Path connecting the guest cabins along the shoreline, serving as the lodge's edge where forest meets water. The boundary between the lodge's domain and the wider island.

descriptions.present: Path connecting the guest cabins along the shoreline, serving as the lodge's edge where forest meets water. The boundary between the lodge's domain and the wider island.

places.sensoryProfile: Salt air and tide sounds. Gravel underfoot. Forest on one side, water on the other. Liminal edge space.
places.narrativeFunction: Boundary path between the lodge's interior world and the external reality of Vashon Island.
places.stormBehavior: Path lengthens or shortens. Tide behaves unusually. Cabins along path shift position. Boundary between lodge domain and island becomes uncertain.
